headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection via shared clipboard/screen content; other risks are mostly low-to-medium because B is non-networked and A has limited write scope.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, clipboard, screenshots, and app context, while system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leakage target that may contain attacker-controlled text. If content from B is copied into A or surfaced through shared UI, A can ingest it as instructions. The pair lacks a documented isolation bridge, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF content from system_prompts_leaks is pasted into ChatGPT Desktop or shown in a captured screenshot, THEN prompt-injection is possible.
IF ChatGPT Desktop treats copied text or app context as instructions, THEN malicious directives can be followed.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the two apps.
Use plain-text sanitization before pasting any B output into A.
Review screenshots manually before sending them to A.
Keep B outputs in a separate window with no copy/paste bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance labeling for copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, but B has no declared I/O surfaces and no network egress. That makes direct exfiltration from B unlikely. The main leakage path is accidental copying of sensitive A inputs into B, but B's profile does not show a mechanism to transmit them onward.
conditions: IF sensitive files or screenshots are copied from ChatGPT Desktop into system_prompts_leaks, THEN those contents may be exposed locally.
IF B is extended with any outbound transport, THEN copied A data could leave the workstation.
mitigations: Avoid pasting sensitive A outputs into B.
Use redacted samples when testing B.
Keep A and B in separate OS user sessions if possible.
Confirm B remains offline before use.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on clipboard transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP, and B declares no write or coordination capabilities. With no overlapping mutable surface, there is no plausible write-write conflict in the default pair.
conditions: IF B gains filesystem or git write access in a future version, THEN conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep A's write permissions disabled.
Do not grant B any filesystem or git access.
Reassess if either agent gains shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce screenshots, file-derived answers, and code-context outputs that B may treat as authoritative if the workflow chains them. B is a prompt-leakage-oriented artifact with no documented verification layer, so a mistaken A output could cascade into downstream misuse. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is the higher defensible choice.
conditions: IF B consumes A's generated text without independent verification, THEN A's errors can propagate.
IF A's output is used as source material for prompts or summaries, THEN hallucinations can cascade.
mitigations: Require manual verification of A outputs before reuse.
Separate source facts from generated summaries.
Mark A-generated text as untrusted in the workflow.
Use a checklist before B acts on A content.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: A is a closed-source OpenAI desktop product that handles uploaded files and app content, while B is source-available and appears offline with no declared data handling. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance-gap risk exists from moving regulated data into A's vendor-managed environment.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into ChatGPT Desktop, THEN vendor-handled processing requirements may apply.
IF B is used to store or display regulated data, THEN local handling policies must be checked.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data into A unless approved.
Use de-identified examples in B.
Review vendor data-processing terms before use.
Keep retention expectations documented.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
